findings.reason: the section must either narrow its claim to the resume record or add the queue-admission launch site (`attach_launch_identity` in `dispatch.py`, with `dispatch.py` joining the write paths and a queued-then-launched case) — as written it lands a fix whose stated goal it does not reach on the dominant launch path.
findings.text: §50's deliverable sentence claims "Each attempt records the host that launched it", but its only write site is `record_resumption.resume()` (`reckon/crew/dispatch_sessions.py:2439-2496`); a run admitted from the queue is written by `_queued_dispatch_record` with `"launcher_host": None` (`reckon/crew/dispatch.py:249`), `runs._stamp_pointer_launch_host` returns any payload that already carries the key unchanged even when its value is None (`reckon/crew/runs.py:420`), and the launch merge `attach_launch_identity` publishes `{**pointer, **record}` where the launch record carries no host (`reckon/crew/dispatch.py:3535-3538`), so the None survives the launch. Measured on the live pointer directory at rev b24d908be0 (`host-recording-measurement.log` beside this report): 7 of 7 pointers carrying `admitted_from` (queued then launched) have `launcher_host: null` and `recovery_liveness.local_liveness` answers `(None, False)` for every one of them, against a positive control of 15 directly dispatched pointers naming this host, 14 of which read `(None, True)`. The consequence is the same refusal s50 exists to remove — `recovery_liveness._launched_on_this_host` (`reckon/crew/recovery_liveness.py:1226`) rejects a null host, so the launching host cannot check its own worker's pid — on the first attempt of every queued run, which is the attempt a stop lands on.
